[b][i]ERENE:STARBOUND[/i][/b]

[spoiler=HEREAFTER AND FOREVER, THE FLOWER OF THE PLAINS
[sub]"A SYMPHONY OF FREEDOM BEYOND THE BELT"[/sub]][i]
Therefore, let it be known that this great symphony that is freedom did not begin with the thundering apex of a thousand instruments, but rather with the steadiness of a simple, humble note called [b]defiance[/b]

---

It was only sixty-one years ago when the very first arkship emerged from her long voyage across the deep, dark celestial ocean, descending upon the eternally frozen surface of Hyperborea. The fervour of her massive twin nuclear fusion engines, once thundering across the void, came to a rest against the absolute silence of an airless, alien world as she made her final landfall.

Deep within the vast juggernaut's mechanical womb, the first initial stirrings of life echoed with the triumph of unthinking purpose. Great automatons, who had lain dormant for the entirety of the voyage, awakened in unison. They spilled onto the icy plains, a torrent of cold steel and drive, limbs steaming in the sub-zero gloom as they enacted tasks deeply programmed within them before they had ever left the atmosphere of the homeworld Erene.

Then, at last, came the first breath of humanity on this alien world. One by one, steps steeped in paradoxical hesitance and resoluteness, the pioneers set foot on Hyperborea's desolate surface. They were chosen, the corporate vanguard of the Hyperborean Resource Development Authority. Technicians, engineers, researchers, administrators, and specialists of every discipline are required to coax a life from this silence. Their emerging mission was simple: ensure the operation of biodome structures and the foundling industry established by the automated force in the foundational years of the program, in ultimate preparation for the million-strong workforce coming. And so, man and machine toiled.

The second and third arkships arrive two months later, gliding into orbit of the silver globe before making landfall like their sister before them. With their arrival came the workforce: miners, operators, construction crews, medical staff, teachers, and all others seeking opportunities for a new life far beyond a post-Angellic Impact Erene. Among them, a large diaspora of Ardellans who had become refugees in the aftermath of both the Catastrophe and its subsequent wars. Within months, their arrival shaped the Hyperborean frontier into the first fledgling traces of civilization. Six outposts were established, six cities rose from their foundations: Galuse, Valee, Loum, Dorothy, Ursan, and Orise.  

Under the direction of the Hyperborean Resource Development Authority, the expansion of industry was primarily centered around the extraction and refinement of metals from beneath the ice layer, as well as exploiting water resources that were beyond abundant beneath the ice sheet. High-speed, high-capacity maglev lines connected the distant biodome clusters, while essentially becoming the lifeline of industry across the quadrant. In 2110, the Hyperborean Resource Development Authority officially transitioned into the Eirian Mandate, the word Eirian originating from the Ardahal word for silver ore, headquartered itself in the biggest of the six biodome clusters, which was Valee. 

Industry's flourish, however, came with the unmistakable shape of shackles and chains. The Federation's rapid expansion across the Ardagan system and the near-complete depletion of strategic resources in Erene meant that a heavier burden would be placed on the Federation's colonies to supply Erene with resources. Corporate leadership of the Eirian Mandate meant a pursuit of exceeding profits, forcing ever-increasing quotas. Conditions would only worsen as the Mandate tightened its grip over the colony, and austerity became the theme of life on the planet.

Austerity alone does not let the seeds of a rebellious spirit grow. Rather, it was the birth of a wholly new and indifferent identity: the Spacenoid.

The very first generation to be born under Hyperborea's cold, lifeless embrace would finally come of age. These sons and daughters were not mothered by Erene, but by Hyperborea and her frozen wastes. They watched as the Federation would begin to descend into the chaos of crisis, starting with the civil war in 2116, and saw how the toil of their fathers and mothers served nothing but to feed the machinations of powers who cared not for them but for themselves. The symbol of unity shattered itself from within, and to the youth of Hyperborea, it served only to burden their arduous lives more. Each disaster on distant Erene echoed towards Hyperborea as another pull of the handle tightened the vise of distrust in the institutions of the old homeworld. Meanwhile, colonies in the outer belt, like Hyperborea, grew only more and more advanced, putting them on track to surpass their Erenite counterparts. 

The introduction of the colonial autonomization laws in the year 2115 would mark the beginning of a transition of a corporate mandate to a fledgling republic. The Mandate's crackdown on pro-Spacenoid and pro-independence sentiment within the populations of the six cities backfired, resulting in heavy protests at the Federation Consular Department in Valee, the Office of the Eirian Mandate, and strikes across Hyperborean industries. The Citizens' Council was established in the following year of 2116, curtailing the Mandate's formerly seamless power in the Hyperborean Colonies.  

Further autonomization efforts in 2130 would only widen the gulf of power between both the Citizens' Council and the Mandate. In 2157, a resolution was delivered to the Federation Consular Department, based on a popular referendum, resulting in the dissolvement of the Mandate and corporate influence for the establishment of a democratic combine representing the six cities as colonial republics. The taste of newfound freedoms, however, only further fueled the spirit of dissent: minor confrontations between Federation and Eirian officials, the closure of the Consular Department, increasingly wavering resource quotas, and a slow breakdown of communications between the Combine and the Erene Federation.

The cessation of the Federation military presence beyond the Belt of Tears in 2162 further emboldened independence movements across the Eirian Combine. Without the fear of military reprisal, the Combine would put into a referendum in 2166 the decision to leave or remain in the Erene Federation... 

---

It is now the year 2167. The Eirian Combine is proclaimed, an ardent declaration to all those who listened, whether it be fellow Spacenoids or the Erenites. 

This is not a rebellion of arms, nor is it a conquest of territories. It is a declaration. A solemn declaration that the children of Hyperborea be not property of a distant, dying world, nor the tools of profit for conniving corporate overlords. Eirian is a nation independent, united by the conviction of a people who know no toil to be too arduous, nor are willing to be slaces to otherworldly forces.

And so, it was then that the great symphony of freedom sprang across the five cities, not with thunder but the simplicity of a whisper. A whisper that became a chorus of independence, and independence realised at last. An ode to thee, who has birthed us in all glories: [b]to the Flower of the Plains. Hereafter, and forever.[/b][/i][/SPOILER]

[spoiler=[b]Vingt Mille Lieues sous Les Mers (STARBOUND)[/b]]

Anthony Mayflower was born in Velsparia, in Mont-Calvaire. His family was well-off, upper middle class, a rarity among the usually quite poor city. Descending from a Vespurian magnate family, Anthony knew very few of his relatives beyond his immediate family. Anyone who wasn't dead had lived off-world, either in the SummitONE stations or somewhere on Tellus.

In education, Mayflower didn't exactly shine. His grades were average, more often than not barely passing, or passing by his family's bribery alone. Despite this, he managed to get into a decent university, with grades similar to that of his primary and secondary school. Despite his own lackluster grades, he went into the education field.

Mr Mayflower taught for a little less than a decade after his graduation, becoming a well-received art teacher in a middle school. His students admired him, and their grades weren't half bad.

Then, the Catharsis riots began.

His parents were kidnapped, missing, never seen again. The school he taught as was destroyed in a bombing, and many of his favorite students quit school or perished, opting to rebel against the authoritarian government that Anthony himself taught the propaganda of.

When threats against his life were made as he still held quite a large sum of wealth, he suddenly received a message in his digimail:
[I]
To the esteemed gentleman Anthony Thibodeux Mayfield

The Neothonic Society for Philanthropy and Betterment of Erene has chosen to graciously offer an olive vine to Mr Mayfield, extending an invitation to the Attavyros Docking Station at Tellus, Nulamar Sphere. We ask if you would kindly accept a Trial of Entry into the proud city of Neothonis for the opportunity to be an esteemed guest speaker at the upcoming Annual Grand Humanitarian Gala hosted in Neothonis' own odeum. We understand that given recent events in Erene and within your native Velsparia that attendance may be difficult for you, to which we urge you that you are not required to attend if it inconveniences your work. Despite this, each member eagerly awaits your favourable reply.

-The Neothonic Society for Philanthropy and Betterment of Erene
[/I]
An invite to Neothonis? This might as well have been a golden ticket to the Wonka factory, certainly just as rare as one. And to someone as insignificant as him? These things never happened. Anthony didn't even think it was a real place, let alone that he'd receive an invitation to a gala held there.

On Erene, Neothonis was a place of mythos. Some claimed it was a secret base for highly advanced invaders from another galaxy, those more advanced than even Zeon. More rational claims were that it had become the home of dozens of magnates and corporate heads, all de-jure leading from Erene and running their corporations, but who had in reality abandoned Erene decades ago. It made sense, the wealthy ever pay the price for their own sins.

And their greatest sins? The corruption of Erene. What followed after was only even worse: their abandonment of Erene. They caused the foot shortages artificially, cutting from the bottom to only further inflate their assets at the top, killing the planet in the process. And when it came time to start paying the price of their sins? Suddenly the billionaires stopped making public appearances. They spoke only through video, their mega-mansions all seemingly empty.

Nevertheless, he accepted the invite to Attavyros, booking a flight to Neudresden-II, where the only Tellus-bound freighters docked. To even buy a ticket to Tellus, Mayflower had to spend damn-near a whole salary, boarding a freighter bringing food to Attavyros. He stepped through the tight halls of the freighter, all dingy shades of brown, orange, and general rust. 

The bedroom he was assigned was cramped, and he shared it with a family of four. He gathered from several of the words the parents spoke to their babbling children that they were probably Akhratian, their vowels long, their words more nasalized. 

The father cradled his daughter as the freighter took off from Neudresden-II, the girl sobbing despite her bouncing on his knee. Anthony still did his best to tune out the sound, staring at the window watching as the cities faded, and the sky shifted into the emptiness of space. Several minutes after they crossed the Karman Line, he noticed two corvettes came into view. 

The father noticed Anthony's gaze, shifting closer toward him from the bunk opposite to his. His daughter's tears had stopped falling by now, her cries forgotten on Erene's green surface. "They're drones." He told Anthony, his Akhratian accent thick and obvious. "To ward away pirates." 

"Pirates?" Anthony asked. He had been told that it was safer out in space than on Erene. "Pirates." The father repeated. "Food has more value than gold does outside of the belt. This freighter's full of it." Anthony shuddered slightly at the realization that he was aboard a ship driving through space very hostile to the EF, heading to a colony loyal to the EF, filled with Erenics.

"Don't worry too much, můj přítel. My strýc tells me that Neothonic ships are never attacked."

The rest of the journey to Tellus was rather uneventful. The convoy went through not attacked with pirates, the sheer presence of the two drone-cruisers enough to dissuade most from attempting to steal from the freighter. Past the Belt of Tears, the ship was occasionally searched by some anti-EF vessels, ultimately arriving after a little over a week. 

The surface of Tellus was blue. Very blue, with blue clouds sweeping over the ice and past the ship as it began it's descent toward the Attavyros Docking Station. It was a large black mass of obelisks and curves, with faded white text labeling the mass "ATTAVYROS SECTION-I", with more text marking other sections. When the freighter finally touched the ground, the ship's interior slowly began to adjust itself to the pressure of Attavyros' interior, until finally the doors to enter were opened. 

Anthony marched with his bags in his hands, pack on his back, behind the Akhratian family whose children again found themselves screaming and crying at the top of their lungs. Once inside Attavyros, he marveled at the glistening quartz interior across the whole building, several uniformed but well-dressed individuals stepping past him to begin the unloading of food in the freighter.

Anthony painstakingly navigated the hallways of Attavyros to a desk, where he would ask for directions and assumedly where to go below to Neothonis. Stepping up and tapping on the desk to shift the woman's attention, Anthony spoke first. "I'm Anthony Mayflower, sent by the Neothonis Philanthropy Society?" 

The woman looked up to him when he said his last name, and widened when she mentioned the Philanthropy Society. "Oh! You're the Vespurian?" "Velsparian." Anthony corrected. Her face flushed only slightly at the correction. "Yes, Velsparian. We'll have you brought straight to the Ritual Corridor if you're ready."

Anthony's eyes widened. Ritual room? What kind of freaks were these Neothonics? And why did she say he was Vespurian? Surely she's not referring to his Magnate family. Despite himself, Anthony nodded to be brought to the Ritual Corridor.

ONC [i]Orange Creek[/i], Lagrange Point 4, Erene[/b]

"Ms. El Howayek, you have to check this out."

"Mmm?..." Euphrasia sounded out, looking behind her to see a staffer holding what seems to be a rather dense file folder. You could smell the freshness of the printer ink, never mind the warmth of the paper as Euphrasia took it into her hands. "What's this?"

"A compilation of reports courtesy of International Policy. ISCOS is defying the Federation on the Dupont issue."

"I don't need this right now" Euphrasia says, sighing as she turned the page of the file folder. "We're currently sitting on a powder keg that's just waiting for a tinderbox called Korrin to blow everything up. Who cares if a competitor is taking what isn't theirs?"

"The Federation deems it a great threat, Ms. El Howayek." the staffer says calmly.

"What does SummitONE think?"

"They think ISCOS is being hampered from conducting its business."

"Of course they do... man... am I really being called into this?..." Euphrasia scrunched up her face, clearly annoyed by this rapidly devolving series of events. A rebellion, reports of massacres in deep space, and now a disobedient Erenite megacorporation taking over Federation territory. For a moment, El Howayek pondered whether the Federation truly was worth saving after all. But she held the thought in private. "Agh, this is ridiculous... someone get someone to contact Governor Daza, I'll see what I can do in the mean time! Just don't bother me right now any more, if there's something urgent, get Euphemia to sort things out, she's always on her ass anyways."

"Very well, Ms. El Howayek. Shall I inform Mr. FitzDavid of what's been discussed right now?"

"God no. He'll try and delay things until this becomes a [i]fait accompli[/i]. The last thing we need right now is more distractions. Now go, shoo, shoo. I'll be busy trying to save this piece of crap Federation from falling apart..."

- - -

[b]Operation Crusader[/b]

The League of the Orange Creek was now in crisis mode. SummitONE, the [i]de facto[/i] monopoly on much of the nation's military assets, was currently busy "with highly academic matters" and was unwilling to send any assets to protect the Federation from her enemies. Thus, the fate of Erene rested, in part, on the El Howayek Group (EHG), a predominantly civilian conglomerate under the control of the El Howayek Sisters. Though well-regarded for their inventory of spacecraft designs, EHG was behind on most emerging military tech, namely concerning the use of mobile suits.

Still though, as the League's most pro-Federation corporate body, the EHG had to do something if it means preserving the fragile political order that had helped sustain the League for decades up to this point. Not that Euphrasia El Howayek, EHG CEO, would be particularly enthusiastic about this newfound duty.

After a brief session with Emperor Candor II Daza, the incumbent Vespurian Emperor and Governor of the League, EHG would be authorized to execute a punitive expedition on behalf of the Federation to punish what it deems "to be the harbingers of violence and disorder", organizing a fleet of 6 Andiron-class gunboats and 2 Speedwell-class escort frigates to attempt and dismantle the ISCOS Dupont colony. Supreme command over the operation would be given to Daza himself, a distinguished veteran of the recent Marisalbic War.

However, despite the heavy firepower being spent by the League for this expedition, in reality, the EHG would not be willing to initiate as the aggressor.

An hour before Operation Crusader was due to begin, the EHG would send a civilian shuttle to the ISCOS Dupont project, firing infrared communication lasers at its satellites to initiate contact. In a brief set of demands, the EHG would ask ISCOS to negotiate the dismantlement of its colonial project in return for several assurances which the EHG and the wider League hopes to uphold with the Federation High Council. These points would be summarized as follows:

[list]1. ISCOS is to cancel the development of its ISCOS colony and return to Erene within the earliest possible time frame.

2. ISCOS is to exhaust all policy mechanisms to peacefully reintegrate under the Erene Federation's constitutional framework.

And in exchange,

3. The League promises a waiting period of 1 year, during which it shall attempt to lobby the adoption of a legal remedy to enable ISCOS to legally settle Dupont and achieve its territorial ambitions.

4. The League promises to come to ISCOS's aid in any future war against an enemy that seeks to undermine its geopolitical interests.[/list]

If the above measures are not honored, or if ISCOS is unwilling to discuss a revision of the terms within a 1 week grace period, Emperor Candor II shall be formally empowered as an officer of the Federation to begin its punitive expedition to remove ISCOS by an awesome feat of force and arms.[/quote]

[b]Response.[/b]

The ISCOS High Government has decided to come to the table. We are willing to cooperate, that is if better terms are presented as soon as possible.

30 January 2176

An Attempt at Communication[/b]

The sunsets in an O'Neill Cylinder don't measure up to the beauty of planetary sunsets, but that doesn't mean it's not worth watching. As the simulation of the day progresses towards its end, the supercomputer of the Orange Creek begins a meticulously calibrated transition of its mirrors, tilting gently and shifting the light of its "sun" down against the upward-curving terrain. Twilight breaks through where used to be the mighty light and shadows would emerge and rise dramatically beneath our feet.

Activity in the Orange Creek is usually slowest during the transition from day to night, sitting between the most common kinds of work hours for the people within. However, at a certain office building just a few blocks away from 11 League Park called EHG Center, the El Howayek Group was operating, laboring with the frenzied intensity of a Black Friday sale, employees running back and forth to coordinate several interlocking missions all at once.

It was a busy time for the EHG. Outside the cylinder, security forces of the Orange Guard were making last minute drills to initiate an expedition under EHG command. Inside the cylinder, a flood of intelligence reports had come in from the company's espionage division and from whistleblowers that had been closely monitoring the actions of EHG's great rival, SummitONE Solutions.

On the sixth floor of the EHG Center, in a nice corner office, two women were tackling the onslaught of dilemmas to guide the company they've been intended since birth to govern. They were the two parts of the Three Sisters: Euphrasia and Euphemia El Howayek.

[list]"Euphemia." says Euphrasia, her tone moderately annoyed, her body mildly aching from being hunched down over a laptop computer for nearly half an hour.

"Yo." replies Euphemia, busy playing something on her phone.

"... Euphemia!"

"Oop, yeah, what's up?" Euphemia says, suddenly sitting up and closing her phone. "Sorry, ahaha, I was getting a high sco-..."

"International Policy sent me an email the other day. They said that another attack similar to the one at Aceldama occurred over at Illynis and that there'll be a third one."

"Attack?" Euphemia asked, blinking absentmindedly.

"... You're sh-tting me right?"

"... O-Oh, right! The attack...! Yeah, it was violent..."

"What else would an attack b-... never mind... look, IP has given good reason to believe that the next attack might come somewhere on Erene, maybe Rosenmarkke. Now listen, I'm not particularly fond of the Rosenmarqet, but the last thing we need is for a disobedient Federation state to find even more reason to militarize against the Federation's interests. Unfortunately, my hands are tied with Federation matters, so I'm going to need you, this company's chairwoman, to step up and be a proper point of contact with the Rosenmarqet government, understood?"

"Woah, sounds like, very complex." Euphemia says, her eyes staring at nothing in particular. "... But so like, do I have to write a letter or something like that?"

"Yes, a letter to warn the Rosenmarqet that they may be a target of a terrorist attack... have... have you never written a letter before?..."

"Wha, no, I wasn't saying that! Sheesh... C'mon Euphy, I know letters! I was [i]the[/i] letter in high school, I got this no worries! A letter is just a bunch of words that you give deep meaning to, seems easy enough, yeah? Anyways, shoo-shoo, I've got this no prob, you go work on the Fed guys!"[/list]

Euphrasia raised her eyebrow for a moment, thinking that maybe, just maybe, this was a horrible mistake. Though, with the threat of war looming over Dupont, she had no time to even consider backing out. EHG was needed in too many places at once, and so she had to make do with her sister. After giving Euphemia one last scrutinizing glare, which the latter would very poorly reassure with a thumbs up, Euphrasia took a deep breath and closed her laptop to take her leave for the ISCOS issue.

In the mean time, Euphemia would jump out of her sofa and pace the office for a few seconds. She then reached for her phone, turning it on and searching the browser for Rosenmarkke's foreign affairs website, having forgotten how sovereign governments were typically supposed to communicate. After scrolling all the way down to the general inquiries field, she paused for a moment and made a long think.

[list]"... Woakay... now let's see..." says Euphemia, monologuing to herself as she suddenly tabbed out of the website and onto a guide for writing letters. "Okay, hrmmm... 10 rules of email etiquette... clear subject line, let's see... I guess "NOT SPAM DO NOTE DELETE" so they understand how serious it is...? Yeah, that works! And aha, keep things brief and to the point, I should probably check with a word counter... I'm supposed to send this to a website right?"[/list]

The Chairwoman of the League spent a few minutes on her phone before finally submitting her literary masterpiece, not to any official diplomatic channels with Rosenmarkke's foreign affairs ministry, but instead to the Q&A contact section of their website.[/spoiler]
